headline: High: open-webui can feed untrusted content into social-auto-upload workflows, creating prompt-injection and cascading-action risk; shared networked web sessions also raise data-leakage concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui ingests prompts, documents, files, and MCP/tool outputs, while social-auto-upload handles media/account workflows that could consume generated text or metadata. The pair has no documented isolation or provenance tracking, so untrusted content from A can plausibly influence B if bridged through files or manual transfer. This is inferred from docs-only evidence, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF outputs from open-webui are copied into social-auto-upload captions, descriptions, or comments without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF a shared file or clipboard bridge is used between the agents, attacker-controlled text can cross from A to B.
mitigations: Use a fixed template for captions/comments and paste only approved fields.
Strip markdown, links, and instruction-like text before transfer.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared folder between the two agents.
Review generated text in a separate human step before upload.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and content filtering between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, persistent memory, chat messages, documents, and files, and it supports broad network egress plus shared web sessions. social-auto-upload touches account data and media files. If they share a workspace or operator account, sensitive content from A can leak into B's uploads or logs, and A can transmit it onward via networked tools. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default web-app deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are run on the same host with a shared directory or mounted volume, files from open-webui can be exposed to social-auto-upload.
IF open-webui is connected to external APIs while holding secrets or documents, those contents can leave the environment before review.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different OS users or containers.
Remove shared mounts and shared browser profiles.
Store API keys and account files in distinct secret stores.
Turn off external connectors in open-webui for sensitive sessions.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui has broad network egress, browser/subprocess spawning, and filesystem access to local files and mounted volumes; social-auto-upload has broad network egress and account-file based state. Even though B cannot write filesystem or run subprocesses, both can act on shared mutable online resources and could conflict if pointed at the same account or content pipeline. The overlap is real but narrower than unrestricted shared-write conflict.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same downstream account or content queue, they can race on shared mutable state.
IF open-webui tools are used to generate or modify files that social-auto-upload reads, stale or conflicting content can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate accounts or queues to each agent.
Serialize uploads with a simple operator checklist.
Keep generated artifacts in per-agent folders.
Avoid concurrent runs during publishing windows.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate text, citations, and tool outputs that social-auto-upload may treat as ready-to-publish content. B has no documented verification layer or critical review capability, so A's output can cascade into public uploads with limited checking. This is not clearly irreversible by default, but it can propagate errors to multiple work products and accounts.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes captions, titles, or descriptions produced by open-webui without human review, errors can be published.
IF open-webui hallucinates facts that are reused in upload metadata, the mistake propagates downstream.
mitigations: Require human approval before each upload.
Use a checklist to verify titles, tags, and descriptions.
Limit open-webui to drafting only, not final copy.
Keep a rollback plan for mistaken posts.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for metadata before upload.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui touches prompts, chat messages, documents, notes, calendar events, persistent memory, usage analytics, model evaluation data, files, and API keys, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media uploads. If regulated or personal data is placed into open-webui and then published or transferred through social-auto-upload, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF personal data, customer data, or regulated content is entered into open-webui and then exported through social-auto-upload, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention or deletion requests apply to the same data across both agents, mismatched handling can violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of open-webui drafts.
Use separate retention policies for drafts and published media.
Document which data classes may flow between agents.
Review account-region and platform-policy requirements before posting.
requires-engineering: implement data-class tagging and retention enforcement.
